A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MACNET and its collaborative scaling study. Their complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Table 1, profile/temperature ablation results, topology-direction comparisons, and scaling experiments in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and scaling results and adds baseline-scaling comparisons and analyses of interaction topics, artifact length, and refinement behavior.

M1.justification: The DAG organization, node/edge role division, topological interaction sequence, artifact-only propagation, and strength aggregation remain. Assistant/instructor become actor/critic. Additional descriptions of hierarchical aggregation and sink handling do not establish a replacement of the earlier procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, HumanEval, SRDD, and CommonGen-Hard with the same task coverage. The new software-development interaction analysis examines an existing domain rather than introducing another dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CoT, AutoGPT, GPTSwarm, and AgentVerse. v2 Section 3.3 additionally reports scaling comparisons using majority voting for closed-domain tasks and best-of-N for open-domain tasks, including voting augmented with CoT or AutoGPT. These were not evaluated comparators in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons that equalize LLM-call counts and a measurement protocol classifying interaction topics and tracking artifact length and refinements. The ablation is now described as removing profiles rather than jointly removing profiles and setting temperature to zero. The stated scaling range changes from 1–50 to 1–64 nodes; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 3.4 and Figure 8 investigate emergence through interaction-topic distributions, artifact length, and adoption of critics' suggestions. v2 also adds topology-density, runtime, and modification-frequency analyses and revises the profile ablation. The divergent-versus-convergent experiment remains, moving from Figure 5 to Figure 6.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 7 introduces explicit vertical error bars, and Table 1 extends significance reporting to comparisons among MACNET topologies. The p ≤ 0.05 threshold is retained. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or the uncertainty calculation, and v2 does not define its error bars.

E6.justification: Table 1 scores and the reversed-topology scores are unchanged, although some significance flags change. The reported ablation drop changes from 2.69% to 3.67% under differently described controls. v2 adds intermediate scaling points, a reported 51.92% runtime reduction for random versus mesh topologies, a 0.9% majority-voting improvement, and interaction-analysis results including 93.10% adoption of suggested refinements. These are added or revised findings, not same-setting benchmark gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds a sink-context token-complexity derivation comparing quadratic and linear growth without and with memory control (Equation 5). It also introduces a Zipf-based tail-token probability and limiting argument (Equation 7). The scaling expression now explicitly uses log node count (Equation 6), substantially extending v1's formal treatment.

C1.justification: The central MACNET, collaborative-scaling, and earlier-emergence claims remain. v2 adds a tentative multidimensional-refinement explanation to the abstract and conclusion and positions inference-time collaboration as a possible shortcut around expensive retraining. Its introduction qualifies baseline superiority to average performance. The irregular-topology advantage was already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of emergence through rare interaction topics, suggestion adoption, and longer artifacts. It revises the density explanation toward longer reasoning versus information overload and discusses task-specific topology suitability and length-sensitive metrics. These add substantive mechanisms and applicability qualifications beyond v1's small-world and propagation-depth explanations.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosure is substantially revised: v2 specifies approximately four default nodes, binary trees, balanced layered structures, random-edge removal, and final-sink handling. It removes v1's GPT-4-generated pool of 4,000 profiles and depth-dependent temperature schedule from 1.0 to 0.0. The access statement changes from a promised code/data release to code stated to be available in the macnet branch; availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning around inference-time computation, reflective reasoning, and agent applications. Newly cited work includes Large Language Monkeys, Graph of Thoughts, cognitive architectures, and numerous medical, educational, scientific, and embodied-agent studies. These are substantive additions beyond venue updates or relocation of related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, evaluation discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 4; topology analysis is reorganized into density, shape, and direction perspectives. Terminology changes throughout from solutions and assistants/instructors to artifacts and actors/critics.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting. Table 1 gains shading and a renamed average column; diagrams and captions are revised. New Figures 5 and 8 display density and interaction-topic analyses. The scaling plots are substantially redrawn with error bars, while the reversed-topology chart is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful support beyond v1's scaling curves through comparisons with equalized LLM calls, the interaction analysis in Section 3.4, and quantitative memory-cost reasoning. These improve the explanation and assessment of the central findings. The net gain is limited by removal of important profile and temperature details and incomplete documentation of the new comparisons and error bars; the main benchmark scores remain unchanged.
